title: Compatible finite affine coproduct maps for locally finitely presented composites
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ and $(h_i:U_i\to X)_{i\in I}$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme] such that every $f\circ h_i$ is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ and $W=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ be affine opens [def-weil-affine-spectrum] with $W\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$. Let $J$ be finite, $i:J\to I$, and let $T_j=\operatorname{Spec}B_j$ be affine open subschemes of $U_{i(j)}$ contained in $h_{i(j)}^{-1}(W)$. Put $B=\prod_jB_j$. The component restrictions induce maps $q:Z=\coprod_jT_j\to W$ and $p:Z\to V$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] satisfying $p=(f|_W)\circ q$. Under the canonical isomorphism $Z\cong\operatorname{Spec}B$ of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum], the maps on rings are the componentwise maps $A\to B$ and $R\to B$; in particular $R\to B$ is the composite $R\to A\to B$. Each $R\to B_j$ is finitely presented [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], $p$ is locally of finite presentation, and $R\to B$ is finitely presented. No flatness, covering, separation or Noetherian hypothesis is required. Empty $J$ and zero rings are allowed, with empty product the zero ring.

source.place: Tag 02KL, lemma-flat-finitely-presented-permanence, proof, replacement by the finite disjoint affine source and the composite map to the affine base; Morphisms Tag 01TQ, lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize.

proof.text: Write $a=f|_W:W\to V$. For each $j$ the assumed image inclusions give restrictions $q_j=h_{i(j)}|_{T_j}:T_j\to W$ and $p_j=(f\circ h_{i(j)})|_{T_j}:T_j\to V$. These restrictions are obtained by restricting the underlying continuous maps and the structure-sheaf maps to the named opens; composition of the restricted sheaf maps gives $p_j=a\circ q_j$. Apply the coproduct universal property to these two families to construct $q:Z\to W$ and $p:Z\to V$. Both $p$ and $a\circ q$ restrict to $p_j$ on every coprojection, so uniqueness gives $p=a\circ q$.

source.place: Tag 02KL, lemma-flat-finitely-presented-permanence, proof: replace the source by a finite disjoint union of affine opens

proof.text: Use the canonical isomorphism e = Sigma.mapIso of the affine-open isoSpec maps followed by asIso (sigmaSpec B). To identify the map induced by q (and likewise p), cancel e.hom and test on every coprojection using Sigma.hom_ext. The identities Sigma.ι_mapIso_hom and ι_sigmaSpec reduce this to the product projection composed with the componentwise ring map, which is the given appLE map by evaluation. Scheme.Opens.toSpecΓ_SpecMap_appLE supplies the required equality. Finally Scheme.Hom.appLE_comp_appLE, evaluated on every section and every product coordinate, gives gamma = beta.comp alpha.

source.place: Tag 02KL, lemma-flat-finitely-presented-permanence, proof: replace the source by a finite disjoint union of affine opens

proof.text: For each $j$, apply the affine-open finite-presentation lemma to $g=f\circ h_{i(j)}:U_{i(j)}\to S$, with source affine open $T_j$ and target affine open $V$. The hypothesis on the composite gives local finite presentation of $g$. The required image containment holds because $h_{i(j)}(T_j)\subseteq W$ and $f(W)\subseteq V$. Its induced ring map is exactly $\gamma_j$ from Step 2. Thus every $R\to B_j$ is finitely presented.

source.place: Tag 01TQ, lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize, (1) implies (2) and the pointwise definition

proof.text: Each restriction (h (i j) ≫ f).resLE V (T j) is locally of finite presentation by the restriction instance. Apply IsZariskiLocalAtSource.sigmaDesc to this family: local finite presentation is local on the source, and the coprojections form an open cover. This proves local finite presentation of p, including for an empty index type.

source.place: Tag 01TQ, lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize, (1) implies (2) and the pointwise definition

proof.text: The coordinate identity of Step 2 identifies Spec.map gamma with e.inv ≫ p ≫ hV.isoSpec.hom. Both isomorphisms are locally of finite presentation and this property is stable under composition, so Spec.map gamma is locally of finite presentation. Mathlib LocallyOfFinitePresentation.SpecMap_iff, the affine finite-presentation criterion, now gives gamma.FinitePresentation.

source.place: Tag 01TQ, lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize, (1) implies (2) and the pointwise definition

proof.text: All constructions use Sigma.desc, Sigma.hom_ext, sigmaSpec, and coordinatewise RingHom.pi identities without choosing an index, so the empty family is included. The source-locality theorem applies to the empty coproduct, and SpecMap_iff then proves finite presentation of the map to the zero product ring. Zero factors cause no change to these arguments. No flatness, covering, separation, or Noetherian assumption is used.
